arabic text: Allah ki behesht ke haq dar asalaam\nAe turbat e Hussain ke zawaaar asalaam
english translation text: Peace be upon the one entitled to Allah's Paradise;\npeace be upon the visitor of Hussain's shrine.

arabic text:
Tujh par salaam sham o sehere zair e Hussain
Zaair hai tere shams o qamar zair e Hussain
Sun keh rahe hai ahle khabar zair e Hussain
Tu tha gunahagar magar zair e Hussain
Tera thikana bar sare aflaak hogaya
Zam zam sadaein deta hai tu paak hogaya

Hajj ka sawaab leke utha tera har qadam
Rakha qadam zameen pe to umrah hua raqam
Aawaz aa rahi hai ye Nabyion ki dam badam
Tu zair e Hussain tere zaireen hum
Deedar kar ke roza e Sarwar ka farsh par
Tune Khuda ko dekh liya jaa ke arsh par
english translation text:
Every step you took carried the reward of Hajj;
when your foot touched the earth, an Umrah was recorded.
The prophets continually call out:
you are Hussain's visitor, and we are your visitors.
By beholding Sarwar's shrine upon the earth,
you have beheld God upon the Divine Throne.

arabic text:
Khola hai rab ne baab e fazilat tere liye
Qudsi bhi kar rahe hai ibadat tere liye
Kawthar hai tere waaste jannat tere liye
Arfeh ke roz hai ye saa’adaat tere liye
Mumtaz kar diya tere masjood ne tujhe

Hajji se pehle dekha hai Mabood ne tujhe
Tujh ko jo aaye Binte Payambar naseeb hai
Qismat ko naaz hai wo muqadar naseeb hai
Tera malayaaka se bhi bharkar naseeb hai
Kya martaba tujhe sar-e-mehshar naseeb hai
Jab nasiran e Shaha ko Khaaliq bulayega
Mehshar mein tu bhi saat bahatar ke jayega
english translation text:
Before the pilgrim of Hajj, the Lord Himself
looked upon you. The daughter of the Prophet
came to receive you—what a destiny! Your fortune is
greater even than that of the angels. What
a rank you will receive upon the plain of
Resurrection: when the Creator calls the helpers of
the King, you too will stand among the seventy-two.

arabic text:
Hajj ke beghair Hajj ka fariza ada kiya
Mausam ki koi fiqar na khauf e qaza kiya
Chahlon se apne marham e zakhme anakiya
Tune payada pa safar e Karbala kiya
Qatre tere paseene ke kya kaam aaye hai
Allah ne unhi se farishtey banaye hai

Kis tarha se bayaan ho manzar wo ishq ke
Paidal jo Karbala ko nikalte hai qaafley
Koi Najaf se aur-koi Basrah ke raha se
Haaton mein yaa Hussain ke parcham liye hue
Zair jo karbala ki taraf dorein jaate hain
Abbas chal ke khud unhe lene ko aate hain
english translation text:
How can the scene of love be described,
when caravans set out on foot towards Karbala?
Some come from Najaf, others from the road of Basra,
carrying standards inscribed 'Ya Hussain'.
When the visitors run towards Karbala,
Abbas himself walks out to welcome them.

arabic text:
Hoti hai ek qataar e mawakib wahan saji
Khidmat mein zaireen ke rehta hai har koi
Pani liye koi to koi ban ke malaashi
Un khadimon ke ishq pe kehta hai dil yehi
Karte hai saaf aa ke paseena jabeen se
Milne Hussain aate hai jab khadimeen se
english translation text:
Rows of mawkibs stand prepared there;
every person remains devoted to serving the visitors.
One brings water, another becomes a masseur.
The heart says of the love of those servants:
when Hussain comes to meet the servants,
he wipes the sweat from their foreheads.

arabic text:
Dulhan ki tarha raaha saja te hai aashiqeen
Khaime mohabito ke lagate hai aashiqeen
Jo saal bhar mein rizq kama te hai aashiqeen
Daulat woh zaairon pe luta te hai aashiqeen
Kehte hai phir bhi qalb humare na bhar sake
Hum zair e Hussain ki khidmat na kar sake
english translation text:
The lovers decorate the roads like a bride;
they establish tents of love.
Whatever sustenance they earn throughout the year,
they spend upon Hussain's visitors.
Yet their hearts still say:
we could not adequately serve the visitors of Hussain.

arabic text:
Jo raaste mein Karbobala ke guzar gaye
Kaise kahoon ke Mir Takkalum woh mar gaye
Pardes mein the laut ke woh apne ghar gaye
Aahe ajal bataoon woh zair khidar gaye
Tare fana se mulq-e-baqa le gaye Hussain
Khud aa ke unko Karbobala le gaye Hussain
english translation text:
O "Mir Taqallum", those who passed away on the road to Karbala—
how can I say that they died?
They were strangers, but returned to their true home.
O messenger of death, tell me: where did those visitors go?
Hussain took them from the land of mortality to the realm of eternity;
Hussain himself came and brought them to Karbala.
